\[ \text{Time} = \frac{\text{Distance}}{\text{Speed}} \]

Substituting the given values (30 miles and 60 mph):

\[ \text{Time} = \frac{30 \text{ miles}}{60 \text{ mph}} = 0.5 \text{ hours} \]

Next, we convert 0.5 hours into minutes:

\[ 0.5 \text{ hours} \times 60 \text{ minutes/hour} = 30 \text{ minutes} \]

Using the textbook's definition of 100 seconds per minute, we convert 30 minutes into seconds:

\[ 30 \text{ minutes} \times 100 \text{ seconds/minute} = 3000 \text{ seconds} \]

Thus, the time taken is:

\[
\boxed{3000}
\]
